Mr Speaker, we have promised Ghanaians that the obnoxious Double- Track system will be abolished in the next two years. Mr Speaker, you were once a member of the Committee on Education, and you knew what was going on. You would realise that it did not help in achieving quality education at all, and that it must be abolished. That one is very important, because school calendars must be the same for all students. They must all go to school at the same time and break at the same time. As I speak now, one year group is at home, waiting for another group to go on holiday before they can also go. That is not the best way to go, and that is why the Minister for Finance and the Minister for Education are promising Ghanaians that in two years, the Double-Track system will be out of the scene. Mr Speaker, it is also interesting to note that this year, we have brought on board 70 private senior high schools as part of the Free SHS programme, and information available shows that it is going well. Next year, we will have it expanded, because once they are on board, we are sure that it is one way to eliminate the Double-Track in our senior high schools. Mr Speaker, when we went to the schools, we saw so many abandoned and stalled projects. Some schools have as many as five, six, or ten projects abandoned at various levels. This Government is determined to make sure that those projects that were started in 2016 in preparation for the Free SHS programme, which their government came and abandoned— They abandoned the E-blocks, the dormitories, the dining hall projects among others. But I can assure this House that work is being done to make sure that these projects are completed, and we will be able to eliminate the Double-Track in the next two years. The Committee expresses its appreciation to the Hon Minister, his Deputy Ministers, Heads of the Agencies and officials of the Ministries of Education and Finance for their support. 2.0 Reference Documents The Committee referred to the following documents during the consideration of the estimates: i. The parliamentary committees identified significant gaps in education funding implementation between 2022 and 2024. However, I don't have enough evidence to determine specific policies discussed regarding education rights and access.

However, some relevant information can be found:

* The Budget Statement provided support structures for teachers, including GH₵1,200 per year for professional development [3cb6ba041032b1ed43eef711033600dce56d3423b1c73255453410a94095e512:108].
* The Committee on Education visited senior high schools and found that the reset agenda in education was working, providing better furniture and addressing other challenges [c3550d590f1c02ab826a61b42b1d6edd4304390ef5191d6da111396f6ee04ddf:5].
* The House approved GH₵29,514,197,713.00 for the services of the Ministry of Education for 2024 [cf93540b99f030653c1d9313ea5f0ed59f3260439bd575a5a3bea87a3e71a4aa:1].

Please note that these points do not directly address specific policies regarding education rights and access.
